title: Biology-Guided Context-Aware Residual Propagation for Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histology
abstract: arXiv:2610.35167v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spatial transcriptomics provides spatially resolved molecular profiling, but its cost, limited throughput and experimental complexity hinder routine large-scale use. Predicting spatial gene expression from hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained histology images offers a scalable alternative, yet remains challenging because histology provides only an indirect morphological view of molecular activity. Existing methods typically decode expression from visual features in a single stage, even when enhanced with spatial aggregation, retrieval or multi-resolution fusion. This formulation is restrictive because spot-level expression reflects not only local morphology but also cellular identity, neighborhood composition and tissue-level organization. We propose BCARP, a Biology-guided Context-Aware Residual Propagation framework for histology-guided spatial transcriptomics prediction. Instead of directly predicting gene expression from histology embedding

translated_title: 生物学引导的上下文感知残差传播用于从组织学图像预测空间基因表达
translated_abstract: 空间转录组学提供了具有空间分辨能力的分子谱分析，但其成本高、通量有限且实验复杂，阻碍了常规大规模应用。从苏木精-伊红（H&E）染色的组织学图像预测空间基因表达提供了一种可扩展的替代方案，但仍然具有挑战性，因为组织学图像仅提供了分子活动的间接形态学视角。现有方法通常在单一阶段中直接从视觉特征解码基因表达，即使辅以空间聚合、检索或多分辨率融合等手段。这种建模方式具有局限性，因为点级的基因表达不仅反映局部形态，还反映细胞身份、邻域组成以及组织水平的结构。我们提出了BCARP——一个用于组织学引导的空间转录组学预测的生物学引导上下文感知残差传播框架。该框架并非直接从组织学嵌入预测基因表达
tldr: 该论文提出BCARP框架，突破传统单阶段直接预测的局限，通过生物学引导的上下文感知残差传播机制，将细胞身份、邻域组成和组织级结构等多层次生物学信息融入从H&E组织学图像预测空间基因表达的过程中。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes BCARP, a biology-guided context-aware residual propagation framework that overcomes the limitations of single-stage direct prediction by incorporating multi-level biological information—cellular identity, neighborhood composition, and tissue-level organization—into spatial gene expression prediction from H&E histology images.
